Q2 and Q3 include Semrush, which added about $480 million of ARR in Q2; excluding it, our illustrative Q2 estimate is about 10.5%. The company's own FY2026 ending ARR growth target is 10.2%, below the signpost. FY2026 revenue consensus of $26.61 billion sits inside the raised target of $26.58-26.63 billion, so no revenue cut occurred.

theses.thesis: T2: Margins hold as AI hosting and inference costs grow, because pricing and mix offset the cost increase.
theses.evidence: Gross margin was 89.6% in Q1, 89.2% in Q2 and 88.7% in Q3. Subscription cost of revenue rose 16.0% in Q2 and 24.1% in Q3 (computed from), against subscription revenue growth of 13.7% in each quarter (computed from). Subscription cost growth exceeded revenue growth in two consecutive quarters, which meets the pre-set invalidation rule. The Q3 gross margin of 88.7% is still above the 88% line.

theses.thesis: T3: The shares are undervalued because the current price implies far less growth than consensus expects.
theses.evidence: Non-GAAP EPS beat consensus by 3.2% in Q1 ($6.06 vs $5.87), 2.5% in Q2 ($5.96 vs $5.81) and 0.7% in Q3 ($6.13 vs $6.09). FY2026 EPS consensus is $24.47, unchanged over 30 days and up 0.6% over 90 days, so there is no headroom above the signpost level. Management raised the FY2026 non-GAAP EPS target in Q2 and again in Q3, to $24.45-24.50. The reverse DCF implies about zero growth at a $91.8 billion enterprise value, and the forward P/E is 9.5x.

theses.thesis: T4: Funding is adequate despite buybacks, because free cash flow covers most of the capital return and debt is manageable.
theses.evidence: Operating cash flow was $2.96 billion in Q1, $2.17 billion in Q2 and $2.52 billion in Q3; the sum of $7.65 billion leaves about $2.35 billion for Q4 to reach $10 billion (illustrative). The current ratio was 0.91x, 0.75x and 0.77x, below the 1.0x signpost. Net cash was +$234 million at Q1, then -$1.44 billion at Q2 and -$1.12 billion at Q3. Repurchases of $2.48 billion, $2.11 billion and $2.23 billion totalled about $6.82 billion, and operating cash flow less capex of about $7.5 billion (illustrative) still covered them, so the invalidation condition is not met.

title: Earnings Review bis Q3 FY2026
headline: Through Q3 FY2026, ASML raised full-year sales guidance to €44–45bn and beat EPS consensus each quarter, while receivables and cash conversion lagged.

theses.thesis: T1: EUV and service growth can sustain revenue expansion above 15% a year as AI capacity spending continues.
theses.evidence: Guidance for FY2026 net sales was raised to €36–40bn in April and to €44–45bn in October. H1 FY2026 service and field option sales rose 28.1%, above the 20% signpost. The Q4 test is not yet due, and EUV system sales are not disclosed separately in the releases, so the EUV invalidation test cannot be run from these sources.

theses.thesis: T2: Margins can stay near 50%+ gross as mix shifts to EUV and service, supporting earnings growth.
theses.evidence: Gross margin was 53.0%, 54.0% and 57.5% in Q1 to Q3, and Q3 was 57.5% against 51.6% a year earlier. EPS beat consensus by 8.0%, 9.1% and 9.9%. On the EU-IFRS basis, H1 gross margin was 50.9%, below the 53.3% of H1 2025, because of capitalised development amortisation; this basis is not the one the signpost uses.

theses.thesis: T3: Customer concentration is a material risk that could cut revenue faster than the cycle would otherwise imply.
theses.evidence: The largest-customer share is not reported in the 2026 quarterly releases, so the signpost cannot be tested before the FY2026 20-F. Unit shipments rose: H1 FY2026 lithography units were 170 against 153. Management said customers are placing orders for 2029 and 2030 and that 2027 and 2028 supply will not fully meet demand, which supports volume but does not change the concentration exposure.

theses.thesis: T4: The current price is fully valued: the shares need growth that history has not delivered for a decade.
theses.evidence: Consensus FY2027 revenue has not been cut: it is €57.4bn, and FY2027 EPS estimates rose 10.5% over 90 days. The valuation inputs are a single snapshot dated 26 November 2026, so they apply to all three quarters. The reverse DCF implies 20.6% annual revenue growth for ten years, up from 20.1% in the baseline, and a 10.6% implied return against an 11.5% WACC. Consensus was raised, so the required growth did not fall; the thesis is not triggered.

title: Earnings Review bis Q3 FY2026
headline: Semiconductor revenue grew 52%, 79% and 127% in Q1-Q3 FY2026, gross margin held at about 68-70%, and FY2026 consensus revenue stayed near $106 billion.

The Q4 guide of $34.8 billion comes on top of nine-month total revenue of $71,089 million, so the full year is tracking close to the $106 billion consensus.

theses.thesis: T3: Gross margin holds near 68% even as AI rack sales grow, so the margin expansion lasts.

In Q3, products reached 82% of revenue against 70% a year earlier and gross margin still rose to 69% from 67%, which tests the compression the annual filing expected. No gross margin guidance was given for Q4.

theses.thesis: T4: Earnings estimates keep rising, so the current valuation stays supported by consensus rather than requiring a higher growth rate.
theses.evidence: FY2027 EPS consensus is $19.33, down 1.0% over 90 days, with 2 analysts raising and none cutting in the last 30 days. It sits 1.7% above the $19 floor, and the analyst range runs from $17.47 to $22.44. FY2026 EPS consensus is $11.65 against $11.62 90 days earlier. At $300.86 the forward P/E is 25.8x on FY2026, well below the 40x invalidation level. All four last quarters beat EPS estimates by 1.3% to 4.4%.

title: Earnings Review bis Q3 FY2026
headline: Mastercard's first three FY2026 quarters: net revenue up 14-16% each quarter, but value-added services growth slipped below the 20% signpost in Q3.

theses.thesis: T1: Value-added services will keep outgrowing the payment network, so blended revenue growth stays at or above 13% in FY2026.
theses.evidence: Reported VAS growth was 22% in Q1 (signpost met, but 18% currency-neutral), 20% in Q2 and 19% in Q3, so the Q3 signpost was missed. Blended reported net revenue growth was 16%, 14% and 14%, and 15% year to date, above the 13% and 12% thresholds. The Q1 status is carried from the thesis log, which recorded it as weakened.

theses.thesis: T2: Operating leverage persists: operating margin stays at or above 57% in FY2026 as adjusted opex grows slower than revenue.
theses.evidence: GAAP operating margin was 58.4%, 60.2% and 59.8%, all above 57%; adjusted opex grew 11%, 11% and 12% against revenue growth of 16%, 14% and 14%. Q2 is the strongest quarter, and Q3 was 0.4 points below Q2 on a GAAP basis. The Q2 strengthening is carried from the thesis log.

theses.thesis: T3: Returns will lag the cost of capital unless revenue compounds near 13.5% a year, because the current price already assumes that growth.
theses.evidence: Nine-month reported revenue growth is 15%, and consensus FY2026 revenue is $37.4 billion (+14.0%) with EPS of $20.06. Consensus FY2027 revenue is $42.1 billion, above the $41.4 billion invalidation line. The share price rose to $659.97 from $646.59 at the 10-K, and the forward P/E is 32.9x, so the price still assumes the growth. The reverse DCF implied growth is 13.8%, above the 13.5% in the baseline (illustrative).

theses.thesis: T4: Regulatory action on interchange and switching is the main threat to growth, and tightening in a major market would push growth below consensus.
theses.evidence: The three filings and releases report no new interchange or switching rule adopted in a major market, and no Regulation II court outcome. Litigation charges were $0, $82 million and $74 million in the three quarters, $156 million for nine months, against $330 million a year earlier, so the FY2026 litigation invalidation threshold of $504 million is on track to be met. Charges were settlements with opted-out US merchants and ATM surcharge complaints, not new rules.

title: Earnings Review bis Q3 FY2026
headline: Q2 issuance surge lifted MCO's margin and EPS; Q3 revenue grew only 1%, operating margin fell 90 bps, and total debt rose above $7.35bn.

theses.thesis: T1: Operating leverage keeps margins expanding, because operating and SG&A cost growth stays well below revenue growth.
theses.evidence: Q2 operating margin rose 480 bps to 47.9% with operating and SG&A costs up 5% against revenue up 15%. Q3 margin fell 90 bps to 44.8% as operating and SG&A costs rose 2% against revenue up 1%, and restructuring rose 29% to $27 million. The Q3 result is the first quarter where cost growth outpaced revenue growth, and the 43.4% signpost cannot be checked until the FY2026 10-K.

theses.thesis: T2: The share price assumes growth well above consensus, so at consensus growth the implied return falls short of the cost of capital.
theses.evidence: Q2 revenue growth of 15% was the strongest quarter, which the logged Q2 status already treats as weakening the thesis. Q3 growth slowed to 1%, below the 9% signpost, which supports the thesis that growth at the current price is not sustained. Consensus FY2026 growth is 6.5% and the reverse DCF implies 18.1% per year.

theses.thesis: T3: Deleveraging continues, but payouts near 94% of free cash flow will limit further debt reduction.
theses.evidence: Total debt was $7,492 million at 30 September 2026, above the $7,351 million FY2025 level and the $7.35 billion signpost. Net cash moved to -$5,871 million from -$5,104 million a year earlier, and cash fell to $1,621 million from $2,259 million. Shares outstanding fell 3.3% y/y. Buyback and dividend dollars for FY2026 are not in the data, so the payout test cannot be confirmed. The 10-Q cites lower interest income from higher repurchases.

theses.thesis: T4: Debt-issuance cyclicality will show up in MIS earnings within a year, so the stock is exposed to a weaker issuance cycle.
theses.evidence: MIS external revenue grew 8% in Q1, 25% in Q2 and fell 1% in Q3. The Q2 surge runs against the thesis's near-term prediction, but the logged Q2 status is kept because the issuance-driven swing in Q3 confirms the cyclicality the thesis describes. The Q3 10-Q cites lower leveraged finance issuance and market volatility as the cause. A full-year MIS decline is not yet visible, so the FY2026 CFG test remains open until the 10-K.
